utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Good morning. Could you take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. If you would like to make yourself comfortable. First of all, you'll be asked some questions by the Office of the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: -- and later cross-examined by Dr. Karadzic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'd first like to ask if 65 ter 90295 could be brought up on the screen, please, but not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, do you see on the screen in front of you your name correctly indicated and your witness pseudonym number in this case?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that for admission under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3798, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, as we discussed, part of your evidence in this case will be submitted in writing and we first need to deal with the formalities associate with that submission. You testified in two trials before this Tribunal and in particular in the Brdjanin case on the 31st of January and the 3rd of February, 2003. And you have subsequently had an opportunity to review the audio recording of that testimony. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I have two matters I wish to clarify with you. The first matter at transcript page 13968, you were asked a question about: "How long in terms of days did the shelling last of Suhaca?" And you answered: "The shelling lasted for four to five weeks." In your Krajisnik testimony at transcript page 2680 to 2681, you said that the shelling of Suhaca lasted a week and stated at transcript page 2718 that there was shooting during a period of several weeks. Can you confirm today how long the shelling lasted of the Suhaca village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The shelling of Suhaca went on for seven weeks, but the whole process from the surrender of weapons to the arrival of Blagaj lasted five to six weeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I just -- the interpretation was that the shelling lasted for seven weeks. Do you mean seven weeks or seven days?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The shelling lasted for seven days.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the shooting lasted over a longer period of time which you've just clarified?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Also transcript page 13968 of the Brdjanin testimony, you said that the shelling was coming from the villages of Josava and Krslje, and in the Krajisnik trial at page 2737, you said that "the Serb soldiers shot at us from the surrounding hills." Can you clarify now whether you mean the shelling was coming from the villages or the surrounding hills; and if so, the surrounding hills of which villages?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The shelling came from the surrounding hills, the hills above Suhaca, from the direction of the village of Josava and the direction of the village of Krslje. Their positions were on the hills surrounding Suhaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The second matter I wish to deal with is when you were asked in the Brdjanin trial about the Suhaca mosque, you stated at transcript page 14012 that it was seven days after you heard the loud explosions, when you were in the village of Blagaj, that two men went to the Suhaca village to bring a man back who had been killed. In the Krajisnik trial at transcript page 2683, you stated it was a day after you heard the loud detonations that the two men went to the Suhaca village. Can you confirm now how long after the explosions did the two men go to the Suhaca village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The same day we were expelled to the village of Blagaj we heard the explosion, the detonation. On the following day, two men went to Suhaca at the request of the Serbian soldiers who asked them to bring the body of the man who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: With those clarifications, can you confirm that the audio recording of the Brdjanin testimony accurately -- is accurate?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, it is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you were asked today about the matters you testified to in the Brdjanin case with the clarifications that you made today, would you provide the same information to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Whatever I stated last time is the truth and I would repeat it today.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, when you say "last time," I'm specifically asking you in relation to your testimony in the Brdjanin case.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, everything I said then was the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, I also note at transcript page 13967, line 11, I think the word "such" should read "search." It's obvious on a reading of that sentence. I tender that under seal, 65 ter 22140A which is the witness's Brdjanin testimony for admission into evidence and 65 ter 22140B which is a public redacted version of the witness's Brdjanin testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, that can be done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 22140A will be Exhibit P3799, under seal; and 65 ter number 22140B will be Exhibit P3800.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And with Your Honour's leave I will now read a summary of the witness's written evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The witness is a Bosnian Muslim from the village of Suhaca in the Bosanski Novi municipality. He testified to the dismissal of non-Serb employees from their employment, the setting up of check-points which were manned by the Serb soldiers, and the surrendering of weapons to the Serb authorities at the end of April 1992. Three days after the weapons had been surrendered, the shelling of the Suhaca village, which was a Muslim village, started and lasted the whole day and the whole night. In the days that followed, the shelling took place in the early hours of the morning. The shelling lasted for a week. The shells were coming from the hills surrounding the village of Suhaca from the direction of the villages of Josava and Krslje and were mostly targeted at hamlets where mosques were located. On the 24th of May, 1992, the inhabitants of Suhaca village were told by JNA soldiers that they had to leave the village. The witness testified that on that day, around 1200 men, women and children left Suhaca. On the same day, all the inhabitants of surrounding non-Serb villages also left the valley. This was approximately 8.000 to 10.000 inhabitants. The witness testified that the convoy of villagers were stopped at the bridge near Blagaj Japra by Serb soldiers wearing JNA uniforms and subsequently returned to the village of Blagaj Japra. While there, the witness heard explosions and received information that the Suhaca mosque was destroyed, and this is scheduled incident D.4. 17 days later Serb soldiers surrounded the village of Blagaj Japra. The witness, along with hundreds of other Bosnian Muslims, was forced into a railroad cattle carrier. The train travelled to Prijedor, where the men aged between 15 and 60 were separated from the women and children. The women, children, and elderly men were taken to Doboj. The train with 700 to 730 men ultimately returned to Bosanski Novi. From the 11th of June, 1992, these men were held captive at the Mlakve football stadium in Bosanski Novi, and this is scheduled detention facility C.4.1. The witness was at the stadium for 46 days. He testified that the detainees were provided with minimal food and water. While detained at the stadium he lost 11 kilos. Detainees were treated roughly and intimidated by the guards. The witness testified that people detained at the football stadium had not been involved in any sort of armed combat. The witness testified that he and other detainees were forced to sign a statement renouncing all of their property and only then were they released from the Mlakve football stadium. While leaving the municipality, the witness saw that Muslim houses and mosques were destroyed. The witness testified that by the end of 1992 not a single Muslim remained in the Suhaca village. That completes the summary of the evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, I have a limited number of questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If -- Your Honours, in the Rule 92 ter notification filed on the 4th of November I listed as an additional exhibit 65 ter 06732, however, this document is part of a Defence exhibit. So rather than create another exhibit I would seek leave to use the Defence exhibit D00470.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If that could be brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, this is a Bosanski Novi SJB report dated the 15th of August, 1992, making reference to the detention of Bosnian Muslims at the Mlakve football stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to the last paragraph of page 2 of the B/C/S document and that's in page 23 -- on page 23 in e-court. And in English it's the first full paragraph on page 3 of the document which is page 19 in e-court. The first paragraph of that sentence -- the first sentence of that paragraph reads: "According to our information, the persons at the collection centre, that is, the stadium, were occasionally permitted visits by their families."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Were your family allowed to visit?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could all the microphones not in use be switched off so we can hear the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they were not allowed to visit me. They were allowed to visit me only on the day when we were to be released, on the last day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The second sentence reads: "The municipal Territorial Defence staff regularly provided them with food which meant one cooked meal a day" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you for slowing down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You stated at transcript page 13999 to 14000 that on the first day you received a quarter of a loaf of bread and one packet of liver paste for four men. And the following day you didn't get much food, only some sort of watery tea. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please switch off microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. The first day when we got off the train and went to the stadium we got one-fourth of a loaf of bread and some cold meat. And on the following days we received even less food and only warm water.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The next sentence of this document reads: "The citizens at the collection centre had at their disposal the use of the football field and the premises of the football club as sleeping quarters." You testified at transcript page 13999 that you slept under the stands for spectators and in one of the locker-rooms. Were you able to use the football field for recreational purposes?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: We were not able to use the stadium for recreational purposes. We were not allowed to move around. We could only move underneath the stands and up to the first half of the width of the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The next sentence reads: "If necessary, they were given medical care ..." You stated at transcript page 14000 that you received no medical care at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to the top of page 5 of the B/C/S document which is page 26 in e-court and the last paragraph on page 5 of the English translation, and that's page 21 in e-court. Halfway down this page it states: "Proceeding from a decision on the voluntary moving out of the citizens issued by the government of the AR Krajina and an order by the Bosanski Novi municipality Crisis Staff on criteria for voluntary moving out, the Bosanski Novi public security station has, in accordance with due procedure, dealt with citizens' requests in the following manner:" And then it lists: "Permanently cancelled residency ... 5.680 persons." And a little bit further down the page, and this is the next page in English, it says: "According to ethnicity the total number of cancelled residencies, Muslims 5.629 ..." And the paragraph below that relevant part -- the relevant part states: "Citizens who have moved out voluntarily have given written statements to the competent municipal organ that their moving was voluntary."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, there are several references there to the voluntary moving of Muslim civilians. Did you voluntarily decide to leave your village of Suhaca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I didn't do it voluntary, neither did any other villager of Suhaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you voluntarily surrender your property to the Bosnian Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I think you said that you were -- at the stadium that you were forced to sign the document; is that correct? This is at transcript page 14014, that you signed the document yourself?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, I signed the document at the stadium under duress before the Serbian soldiers who were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: A little below it, it states that: "On the 23rd of July, 1992, 6.000 citizens in 50 buses, 11 freighters, 12 trucks, and 200 passenger cars joined the convoy moving out of the territory." What day did you leave the stadium?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: On that same day we left the territory, the city of Bosanski Novi, and the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said -- at transcript page 14017 you made mention that you got onto buses and trucks. Did you also see freighters and this large number of passenger cars in the convoy when you were leaving the Mlakve stadium and Bosanski Novi municipality?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: As I was waiting at the stadium for my turn to arrive, we could see a long convoy forming on the main road in the direction of Dvor and Kostajnica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I wish to turn briefly now to another topic. At transcript page 14012 to 14013 you testified about the damage that was done to the Suhaca mosque, and I want to ask you about certain other mosques. And I'll simply read the name of the mosque and if you could please tell us what condition it was in when you left in 1992, and if it was damaged, if you know when and by whom. And I would like you to keep your answers as brief as possible, please. The mosque in Blagaj Japra?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The mosque is Blagaj Japra was already damaged on the day when we arrived. The minaret, the bell-tower, was heavily damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The mosques in Prekosanje, Urije and Gornji Agici?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I couldn't see the mosque in Gornji Agici. We couldn't go in that direction. As for the mosque in Prekosanje, I saw it on my way back from Ostruzna. I could see it from the train.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was it damaged?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The minaret was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the mosque in Urije?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The mosque in Urije, that we could see from the train across the River Sana also. The minaret had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The old wooden mosque in Blagaj Reka?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: That mosque was torched while we were still in Blagaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you witness this?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, I saw two soldiers in a civilian car who set the mosque on fire because it had a wooden minaret.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And when you say "two soldiers," do you know the ethnicity of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I was not close to them. They were probably Serbs. They were in military uniform. All the Muslims were in Blagaj. We could not even cross the bridge to go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the town mosques in Bosanski Novi, that is, the Gradiska dzamija and the Vidorija mosques?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I saw those two mosques before I left the stadium. We were travelling in an open-top lorry and we could see very well that Vidorijska mosque was damaged, the minaret had been destroyed and the roof had been set on fire. And the city mosque was completely destroyed and most of the -- most of it was razed to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And final the Stara Suhaca mosque?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Suhaca had two mosques. When we left they were both intact; however, after that detonation people went there to bring the man's body and they saw that the Brcanska [phoen] mosque in Suhaca had the minaret destroyed and the main mosque in Dzemat also had its minaret destroyed. They couldn't pass on that road. They had to leave the car and proceed on foot.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, now your opportunity to cross-examine. We'll stick to the original time-scale, so we'll break at 12.30, if you would like to take that into account when structuring your cross-examination. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honour, I seek to tender the associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: So be it, those will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just note that we didn't receive the allocation of our time for this cross-examination until this morning, so in terms of structuring the cross-examination it was difficult to do that because we didn't know how long would be allowed. So if you would take that into consideration if Dr. Karadzic needs some additional time, we would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: All those things will be considered on their merits, Mr. Robinson. I do appreciate it was a late notification.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to ask you a few unusual questions briefly. The answers you gave to the questions put by the Prosecutor here and also in the transcript that was admitted, is that true? Was that correct? Is there no exaggeration there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, that is true, there is no exaggeration whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it the whole truth?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Well, there are a few other things too, but these are minor points that are perhaps not of interest here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The distinguished Madam Sutherland asked you to give brief answers. Can I count on brief answers too?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No problem, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I also count on what you are going to say is going to be true?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: As I said, nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Muslims in your area organised themselves militarily and armed themselves already in the beginning of June 1991?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that from the central level of the party, the Una staff was ordered to be appointed and Bosanski Novi belonged to it too?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could it have happened that the arming went on without you knowing about it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: In my village and in the valley of the Japra, I certainly knew what was going on. So that is something that was transferred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the first victims in your municipalities were Serbs in Bosanska Kostajnica who already in September 1991 suffered from shells coming from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Well, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the war in Croatia was very close to you, basically on the other bank of the Una river?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: That is correct. It could be felt too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could it be felt because shells were coming there and sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, not because of that, because of the soldiers who would come from the front line and then create problems and open fire. Sometimes we couldn't sleep all night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you saying now that there was no shooting whatsoever from Croatia in 1991, no shooting at the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and you in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Not in the Japra valley. I do not know directly for Kostajnica or the town of Bosanski Novi because our movement was restricted already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that in 1991 somebody restricted your movement at the time when there was no war in our area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes. During the day we would move about freely. After 7.00 p.m. they had certain check-points where we were checked, maltreated, and that is why we avoided moving about at that time unless it was absolutely necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're talking about 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, already in 1991 they were in military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was in power in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1991?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I do, yes. Is that necessary?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know who the minister of the interior was in 1991?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I know that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber, give us the name and the person's ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Do I have to? It was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Alija Delimustafic; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He comes from your area, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: He's a Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm saying now that it's not correct, that in 1991 there was a force that would do that to you. Even if that did exist, the entire world would have known about it and the Assembly would have discussed it. Why are you bringing in 1991 as this year of restrictions?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Because I personally was checked at such check-points between the village of Rozici and Donji Agici, near the so-called Mala Ravska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Checked by who?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Serb soldiers, and the main one was Gojko Davidovic, who worked for the municipality as a clerk in Donji Agici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify this now. Was this happening while Bosnia was still in Yugoslavia and while the JNA was fighting in Croatia on the other side of the river?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does the main road go through your village or close to your village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it goes through my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, coming from Sanski Most or Prijedor, this road I mean?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Prijedor-Bosanski Novi is the main road that could be used to reach Sanski Most as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So let us be very specific. The war is on the other side of the river. The area is close to this area. So you're checked by the JNA, not by the Serb army; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I was checked by local inhabitants of Donji Agici who were ethnic Serbs and wearing JNA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that in September 1991 Serbs from your area responded to the JNA call-up en masse and that they were the ones who were checking you, these were the mobilised reservists that I just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, these were reservists who went to the Croatian front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we've clarified that, yes. In your statement you said, you said -- as a matter of fact, you said that in the Krajisnik case and in your statement in the Brdjanin case. You said that the SDA won in Bosanski Novi. Is that correct or is it correct that it was the SDS that won in Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The SDA won in Suhaca and the SDS won in Bosanski Novi because at the time there was Kostajnica and Bosanski Novi as a single municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In Bosanski Novi were there two times more Serbs than Muslims almost, 25.000 Serbs, 1.500 Yugoslavs, and 14.000 Muslims?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Possibly, but as I said, because Kostajnica was also part of Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Whereas you and Suhaca had how many Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since when? According to the census you had nine Serbs. What happened to them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No. Maslovare and Josava and Uzice are the villages that had those nine. Suhaca as a village did not have a single one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The census says that there were 1.070 Muslims, there were -- no, no. Four Serbs and nine were in Svodna. So there were four Serbs, one Yugoslav, and the rest 1.077 were Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: That's what the census said, but most of the elderly inhabitants said that they were Yugoslavs or that they were undecided. Some even said that they were Serbs although they were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why do you think a Muslim cannot be a Serb?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I didn't say that they cannot, but that is what the papers said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I think that this had to do with those Yugoslav communists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that in the beginning of April 1992 a Crisis Staff was established in Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: In Bosanski Novi, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that on the 15th of April, 1992, the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly asked for different goods to be bought and that they should be located in particular areas in order to feed the population?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't know. We did not get anything up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that towards the end of April in Bosanska Krupa, which is your neighbouring municipality, there were armed conflicts?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that on the 4th of May, 1992, negotiations started between the SDS and the SDA at local level. What was discussed was the preservation of peace and the disarming of unlegally armed groups.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Perhaps there were negotiations, but we were in Blagaj by then. We had already been expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 4th of May?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that on the 4th of May all illegally armed individuals and groups were asked to surrender their weapons to the TO staff by the 11th of May at the latest?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, but we had already resolved that, and on the 11th of May I was at the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that in Blagaj on the 9th of May there was a meeting of Dzafer Kapetanovic and Nesmir Ceric, operatives who elaborated a plan to liquidate Serbs in the municipality of Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. On the 9th of May we were loaded onto a train.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you're probably going to say that you don't know that between the 10th and 11th of May in Blagaj Rijeka, the military police patrol was attacked by armed Muslims?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Between the 9th and 11th of May we were on that train in Ostruzna and I don't know about this at all. I don't know who could have done that because there were no Muslims left there. There were only three families left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm asking you about your knowledge, to see what it is that you know. That is very important for me. You can feel free to say whatever you wish to say. Did you hear of the Bosanski Novi staff ordering a cease-fire on the evening of the 11th of May and the continued implementation of the decision stating that the police and TO should continue collecting weapons?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. I was detained at the stadium from the 11th of May onwards, and from that day onwards I did not hear anything, I did not know about anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll go back to that. Let us now see whether you knew that on the 12th of May the Crisis Staff warned against looting and said that measures should be taken to prevent looting?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: As I've already said, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that from Donji Agici and Gornji Agici, on the 12th and 13th of May citizens formed a column to leave their village and they set out towards Prijedor and Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, most of the citizens of Gornji Agici, they set out in the direction of Prijedor and Sanski Most. Part of them even joined us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. No doubt that at the time both Prijedor and Sanski Most were in Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Also there is no doubt that Prijedor and Sanski Most are further away from the front line in Croatia, further away from the Una river; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find out that on the 13th of May the Crisis Staff dissociated itself from the activity of groups that were out of control and ordered to have the terrain searched and to have them arrested in order to create conditions for the return of the population that had fled?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. I was at the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also don't know that on the 15th of May the Crisis Staff passed decisions to continue disarming paramilitaries and persons who were illegally armed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't know any of that. As I've already said, we were not informed about anything at the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the Municipal Board of the SDS on the 20th of May held a meeting and adopted certain conclusions, stating that all citizens who wished to leave Bosanski Novi should be allowed to do so and the authorities were asked to ban all activities aimed at expelling the population?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt, but it's a matter that I would want to re-examine on and I think it's probably best that it get cleared up right now. In the witness's transcript at page 13998 he says that he went to the football stadium on the 11th of June, 1992, not the 11th of May. And I think that there may be some confusion and he's a month out. And I -- in fixing it in re-examination, then Mr. Karadzic would want to then re -- further -- further cross-examine because of all the answers that have been given up until this point. So I think it's -- it might be helpful to clarify it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I agree, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had intended to clarify that, but I wanted to take care of this stage of my cross-examination. It's quite clear to me that it was in June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you agree that it was June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do agree. It was June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the dates are the 9th and the 11th of June. They're actually the same like the 9th and 11th of May, as Mr. Karadzic was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that the 9th and 11th of July and August and September and whatever are all the same.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, but the situation that I described, the 9th leaving Blagaj, the 11th ending up in camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: June?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in May you were in your village, you had electricity, access to the news, and so on?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: We did not have any electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about transistor radios?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Well, it depended on who had batteries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that on the 21st of May the representatives of the SDA and the SDS discussed the conclusions of the SDS of the 20th of May; namely, that the SDS had handed over their conclusions and they met up together in order to look at these conclusions to see whether the SDA had any objections?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I just know that while we were in Blagaj, a member of the SDA went to Bosanski Novi, and every time he would return he would say, "We didn't manage to resolve anything."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. They did not inform you that the SDA, on the 21st of March, accepted the policy of the SDS and also the positions that were agreed upon, the conclusions of the SDS on the 20th of May?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that on the 24th of May, the Muslim population assembled in the central part of the village of Blagaj Japra?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that on the 25th of May, the Crisis Staff ordered the municipal TO staff to urgently place under control all armed individuals and units and to use the military police to arrest those who were not under control and to disarm them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't know that. The people who resided in Blagaj were not armed. The disarmament process had already taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that following the order even greater chaos occurred and that there were more groups and individuals which were no longer under control; in other words, they were infuriated by the Serb authority's decisions?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in your municipality certain policemen were killed in Prijedor during an attack by the Green Beret Muslim forces on the town of Prijedor on the 29th, 30th, and 31st of May; and that there were funerals in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I know about the funerals, but I don't know where those people had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that on the June 1st, in the evening, following the funeral of a policeman killed in Prijedor, there was combat in the settlement of Prekosanje? There was a clash between armed Muslims and armed Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that on the 2nd of June, the TO of Bosanski Novi and the military police evacuated the residents to the stadium for the duration of the fighting. They assembled them at the stadium?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that it was a legal obligation on their part under the Law on All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: As far as I know - and a relative of mine was there at the stadium at the time - was that there were searches of Muslim houses. And a few days later they were returned to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A few days, exactly, on the 4th of June. It was then that the municipal Crisis Staff ordered the municipal TO staff to release all those who were held there, save for a number of perpetrators. A few Muslim extremists were held back. You don't have to agree with me when I say that they were extremists, but there were a few people who were retained. Those were deemed to be extremists by the Crisis Staff. The rest were released. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't know if they kept anyone. The rest were sent home and they were not guarded by either civilians or soldiers. They were simply brought to the stadium, where they spent a few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Military police data indicated that 17 people were kept in the premises of the military police, and that is perhaps why you were unaware of it because the number is relatively small; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: That is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 8th of June the residents of Blagaj went towards Banja Luka in an organised fashion?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: That is not correct. We did not leave of our own accord. Your request was sent to -- was to either go to Bosanski Novi or across the river to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who prevented you from crossing the river into Croatia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The Serb authorities of Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then on the 11th of June, since around the 8th of June or 9th of June 22 railway cars were filled up, how many railway cars were there exactly and how many people were placed in those cars and where did they go to?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: In Blagaj there was a total of around 8.000 people. On that day we were driven out by soldiers wearing JNA uniforms. We were sent to the bridge which they controlled. And from there we went to the Japra factory. We were checked there again. They removed a few people and the rest were placed on railway cars which went to Banja Luka -- towards Banja Luka. We arrived at Ostruzna, near Doboj, where we stopped for two hours without anyone being around. Then soldiers reappeared and some 750 people were placed on board four railway cars. Those cars were returned back to Bosanski Novi and the rest of the train went on to Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the soldiers know that you asked to go to Croatia? Were they informed of that and was it contrary to your wishes that they sent you to Doboj?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: They did know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you repeat your request to them, saying that you did not wish to go to Doboj but across the river to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: We did. But they said, "Well, this is another route you can take to Croatia."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that Doboj at the time, as now, was in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The borders did change, but I think it was the case even back then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many cars were there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Four railway cars were returned to Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no. When the whole train started off, how many people were placed in how many cars?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: It's difficult to say. There were around 7.000 people, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And let's say there were about a hundred people per car?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: More.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This would mean that there must have been between 70 and 80 cars; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, if the math is correct, but there weren't as many cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, a railway car is about 16 metres in length. If there were 60, what was the entire length of the train? Between 900 and 1.000 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The train was not that long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I was trying to ascertain something. Do you agree that a train longer than 500 or 600 metres could not move along that railroad line because its technical characteristics would not allow it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The train --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many of the 700 returned? Did you say one-third?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The answer was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that a longer train could not move along that line; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, due to the technical characteristics of the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you say anywhere that approximately one-third of those of fighting age were returned?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Between 700 and 750.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree then that there must have been four -- or less than 4.000 people and not between 7 - and 8.000?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: In Blagaj there were 7- to 8.000 people, whereas the cars which went to Doboj had around 4- or 5.000 people. During the stay in Doboj, some of the people went to Bosanski Novi to stay with their relatives. There simply wasn't enough space in Blagaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So they did that on their own?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, and for the most part there were children and women doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it unsafe to stay in Blagaj at the time, given the fighting and people who were out of control? Was it unsafe?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: It was, and there was firing from the direction of Petkovci, but there were nowhere for us to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was anybody killed at the stadium, was fire opened at the stadium in Mlakve?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No one was killed at the stadium, although there was firing, whenever soldiers passed by on the road nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They fired in the air?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, they cursed, they fired, and in those situations we were told by the guards to hide under the seats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that the guards were trying to protect you from those passing by?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, from the soldiers who were passing by, they would try to give us cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude then that there were more of you there and that you were safer there and guarded there, which was not the situation in Blagaj?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: That's a good question. I felt safer in Blagaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that at the time of your stay at the stadium, the Posavina corridor was closed, in other words, there was no link between Bosanska Krajina and Srpska Krajina as well as Semberija, there was no traffic? The corridor was cut off?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I didn't know it then, but later on my wife told me that she went a good part of the road on foot because the rest was closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that the fighting for the corridor took place on the 28th of June and the corridor was unsafe until a few months later, perhaps up to September?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't know any of that. While we were at the stadium we had no information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Given all that, did you learn that there was a shortage of food and that the shops were no longer being supplied from Serbia because of the situation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware that the 7- or 8.000 of you -- that providing at least a single meal for each one of you was a very difficult task; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I would, but if you looked at how much food and supplies we left back at Blagaj, it would have been enough for four or five months for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said you slept in the changing rooms and on the seats. Are these standard facilities on a soccer pitch?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, there were changing rooms and showers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, you had access to the showers and water?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, we only slept there but there was no water.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But there were showers, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, but there was no water. We basically used the facility to dry our clothes off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said somewhere that en route through the town you saw the Orthodox church was intact; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that it was built after the war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't know which one you mean. The one I saw existed before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your testimony in the Brdjanin case, on page 13595 you said that the relationship between the Serbs and Muslims in Suhaca were good, that you played soccer and associated with the Serbs in Suhaca as well as with the Serbs from Josava, but the relationship was disturbed once the war in Croatia began. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we agree that there is a significant difference -- there came a significant change when the mobilisations began taking place and when Croatia seceded?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes. The Serb residents were drafted, mobilised, and equipped, and as of that moment they no longer remained in touch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the Presidency of B&H and the SDA ordered their followers not to respond to any JNA calls?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree they didn't -- they didn't respond to either the June or September calls by the JNA, the Muslims and Croats simply failed to respond?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you a military conscript?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I had been before the war in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you respond to the mobilisation call?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: During that period there were no further reserve mobilisations. Once I completed my compulsory military term, I was no longer under the obligation to keep my uniform. I was no longer obliged to do that under the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement of the 11th of December in the Brdjanin case -- it is actually your testimony on page 00 -- sorry, no, it is indeed your statement of the 11th of December, 1998. The page is 00672865, paragraph 8, as well as in your Brdjanin evidence on the 31st of January, 2003, on page 13961, you say that following the elections and during the war in Croatia but before the war in Bosnia the Serbs began firing people from their jobs. Can you tell us whether it is correct. Did it indeed take place in 1991 during the war in Croatia? Were Serbs laying people off?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, in late 1991, three people in Bosanski Novi were dismissed from work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Two civil -- public servants and a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why were they dismissed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I know of them -- one of them personally and he told me that he was dismissed only because he was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Hmm. Well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 65 ter 6706.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that a joint MUP existed up to 27 or 28 March 1992?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: The MUP existed, whether it was a joint organisation or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please pay attention to the report on the current security situation and the circumstances of reserve police forces mobilisation. The report was issued on the 11th of July, 1991. And there is a reference here in the first line to the recent events in Slovenia and Croatia, and it says that in the municipality of Bosanski Novi, Bosanska Dubica, Bosanska Gradiska and Srbac, bordering with the territory of Croatia, the security situation has become drastically complicated, thus taking the characteristics of a state of emergency and even of war. Is it therefore correct that even before the war in Croatia as a result of announcements of the events in Croatia and Slovenia, this is how the police assessed the situation in several municipalities bordering on Croatia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: It is true that in 1991 there were two Muslim police officers in Suhaca. They patrolled the area during the day and they represented the MUP of Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're saying that in Suhaca -- or rather, that the police had sent two police officers to Suhaca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, they were reserve policemen because none of the Serbs wanted to patrol the area. Serbs patrolled the area in the Serbian villages, Muslim patrolled around Muslim villages, and that's how we received these two men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you're saying that the Serb police already in mid-1991 patrolled Serbian villages, whereas Muslim policemen manned and patrolled the Muslim villages, and that all that was done with the blessing of the police station and this was done with full understanding of the police and the population?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes. Those two police officers patrolled the village of Suhaca as I've told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at the text and you will see how the situation is characterised. It says that due to a continuous reflection of all known incidents on the territory of Croatia, a few special forces of Croatian MUP have been noticed on the border, rumour is spreading -- were there rumours at the time that intimidated and irritated the population of all three ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I heard rumours, but according to those rumours the situation was rather bad in Croatia. There was fear of fighting going on. It would spill over into Bosnia, and we could feel that when the combatants returned from the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, they did not return in June and July?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: You mean from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to wait and I'm kindly asking you to wait for the interpretation to finish. On the 11th of July they were still not returning from Croatia, and if you look at the report you will see that the report speaks about high tensions among our peoples in the municipalities along the border because of the events in Croatia. It says here that there is fire being opened from automatic weapons from Kozibrod, Uncani, Struga, all in the territory of Croatia. Were you aware of all that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that. I'm talking -- I'm speaking more in general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it says here that occasionally fire would be returned from Bosanski Novi which means that fire was returned from your municipality. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. Suhaca is 8 kilometres away from the border, so I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I go to the following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you really base everything you know only on what you saw in Suhaca? Did you know anything that was going on in the entire municipality and the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Most of what I know comes from Suhaca, the valley of Japra, Blagaj, the train, and the stadium. And as far as Bosanski Novi municipality is concerned we only heard things. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, if it's convenient we'll break now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: We'll break now until 1.30. Thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.31 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have this document admitted? It is the one from July 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1911, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, let me check something. So you don't know whether only the two were fired and why, except that one of them told you that he had been fired for being a Muslim; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that some Serbs were laid off too?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at 65 ter 6697 in e-court. Can you tell us first who were the Muslim leaders in Suhaca, do you know their names?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Sifet Barjaktarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Adem Barjaktarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Adem Barjaktarevic is one of the people who were fired; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is mid-April, Banja Luka, national security, it discusses --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have a translation? We should. It seems we don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is a security situation assessment in Bosanski Novi on the 16th of April. Apparently at that moment in time, the inter-ethnic relations were complex with divergent views in the way the escalation in violence is interpreted. There were clashes among paramilitary formations, self-organised citizens, and JNA units throughout the republic. The second paragraph, the momentary -- the balance in the situation is contributed by a cessation in military clashes and the arrival of peacekeeping forces in Banja and Western Slavonia, where many mobilised citizens from the area of Bosanski Novi acted as part of JNA units. In April when the UN arrived in Croatia, the tensions were eased, at least for a while; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I see this document for the first time. As for the situation in Croatia and the -- and its influence, I wasn't familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph we have a mention made of escalating war-time conflicts, permanent aggression against units and barracks of the JNA in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the presence of Croatian paramilitary forces (HOS and ZNG) in the outskirts of our general region, in keeping with personal and property insecurity experienced by the citizens at the general collapse of the economy ..." and so on and so forth. By that time the war in Croatia was underway, and were you familiar with the fact that there were armed groups of ZNG members in your area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I was not familiar with that. In the valley of Japra, in the villages there, there were no armed clashes or any other soldiers, save for those of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have this admitted, as it is a list illustrative of the events at the time? I believe we'll have to have it marked for identification. I really did think we had a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1912, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I don't think the Trial Chamber had ruled yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 65 ter 6736.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the Patriotic League was established in Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 13th of April, and did you know that in your area the Patriotic League and Green Berets had their units?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I wasn't familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a review of security findings in the area of the Assembly of municipalities in Bosanski Novi concerning illegally obtaining, possessing, and using fire-arms and forming military organisations under the command of the SDA. The date is the 18th of May, 1992. Let's see what it says. "In Bosanski Novi, due to the conflict in Croatia in late 1991 and early 1992, the situation is characterised by deteriorating relations which are coming to a head between ethnic groups. During the above-mentioned period, SDA activists started organising Crisis Staffs and forming military organisations whose purpose was to fight the Serbian people in the JNA and TO units with the final objective of establishing, in accordance with official SDA policies, an independent state of Bosnia-Herzegovina." What do you have to say about this?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Nothing. We were not privy to any political developments. We were simply told there was a war in Croatia, which we could feel ourselves, and that nothing good would come out of it for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can see at the top it says that on the 12th of January, in the house of Vehid Huzejrovic -- do you know him? He's from Blagaj Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: It does ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say a meeting of SDA activists was held which took six hours, and the activists arrived from Agici, Suhaca, and Blagaj Japra, totalling 14 people. The meeting was presided by Dzafer Kapetanovic and Resad Berberovic. Do you know the two?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, they are from Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. They discussed the creation of an armed formation commanded by the SDA with its seat in Blagaj. And the next paragraph, on the 23rd of February we see Topic Alaga from Cazin. He attended a meeting where there were about 160 SDA activists. He stated that the SDA official policy and that of the senior members of the Islamic religious community must advocate living together with the Serbian people in this territory but that military organisations had to be fortified or strengthened at the same time.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of this. Where was this held?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the community hall in Blagaj Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at March and April, then. It says: "In Blagaj Rijeka, Sefik Velentalic ..." do you know him?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "... with the help of his wife Vesna and a certain Zdenka, both employees of the medical centre in Bosanski Novi, worked on preparing and organising medical care for the SDA military group in case fighting broke out with members of the TO and JNA." Then it says that Agrokomerc trucks were used to bring in five mortars, two or three anti-aircraft guns, a machine-gun, and so on and so forth. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I did not. I was discussing only the valley of Japra and no such things took place there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But Blagaj is not far away, is it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then it says that data was received about the position of automatic weapons and we have a list of 20 people who were involved in that armed organisation. Do you know any of them? (redacted) (redacted) No, you don't need to say that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have that redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see Mr. Sisic, a hodza from Burim? He too seemed to have taken part in the arming process --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, it might be better if you just let the witness read through the list and then ask him a question as to whether he knows any of them and deal with it on that basis.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you have a look at the list and tell us if you know any of the initial 12 people?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I do. Not all of them, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 2, is it not a hodza who took part in that military organisation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't know that people -- that person and I don't know if he was a hodza or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, look at the rest of the list, do you know anyone?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I do know one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move on to the next page. We have Ibro Selimagic and Vehid Husejrovic who kept documents and lists produced by the SDA. Can we go to page 5 immediately since we don't have much time. This regards Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you read the first paragraph so that we would know who is at the helm of the military wing of the SDA. Do you want me to read it out?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: You wanted me to read it out loud?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: "At the helm of the military organisation of the SDA are Izet Mehmedagic, Ismet Muslimovic, Resad Berberovic, and Azemir Ceric. Organising things in the field are Dzafer Kapetanovic, Sejad Ceric, Hajrudin Grudic, and Kasim Falan. In the area of Bosanski Novi, an office was established in order to gather data about JNA units and political and security-related decisions of the official -- official authorities of Bosanski Novi and the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So we have some familiar names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: One moment, Dr. Karadzic. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I was just wondering why the witness was needing to read it out and why simply a question couldn't be put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I think it's going to be now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You know Mehmedagic or at least you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm running out of time. The entire document is quite precise in terms of dates and places where people were. Mehmedagic is also mentioned in relation to arrests; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have this admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on what the witness has testified to, there doesn't appear to be a basis at the moment. He simply agreed that he knows a couple of people that are named in the document, and then he read a passage when he was asked to by the -- by the accused. So it may be that this isn't the right witness to put this document to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, that must be right, mustn't it, Dr. Karadzic? It cannot be said that this witness has adopted the document or confirmed any material aspect of it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Although it seems to me that this is relevant because the document was produced at the time and concerns the events surrounding this witness. So it's important whether he knew about those events or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Microphone again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I was just going to say I would also ask -- respectfully ask Your Honour to reconsider admitting the last two documents because also on the basis of what the witness answered in relation to the first document dated July 1991, there really is no basis to have it admitted. And that was the one we dealt with before the lunch break or the one just previous to this document, given the witness -- what the witness had testified to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me. Yes, Mr. President, I think this is an example that we've encountered before where even though the witness may not adopt the document or significant parts of it, it deals directly with events that -- in his municipality that he might be thought to -- ought to be aware of and reflects on his credibility, the fact that he denies knowledge of all that. I think in the past we've taken the position that documents which contradict the testimony of the witness or which deal directly with things involving the witness or something he would be expected to know can also be admitted. We're not only admitting consistent documents -- documents consistent with his testimony, but we admit documents that are pointed and affect the witness and also are not consistent. And I think this falls within this category, these -- all three documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Certainly in respect of the first two documents that were admitted, D1911, the one dated July 1991, and the previous document, D1912, none of the answers the witness gave you could actually say that -- that it would reflect on his credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, speaking for myself, I find that a difficult concept to embrace in terms of what the witness actually said in respect of the document. But I'll consult with my colleagues, but can we move on now and we'll deal with this matter in due course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to call up 65 ter 6709.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the third paragraph. Kapetanovic and -- attended a meeting in Blagaj to discuss the plan to expel and execute Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here it says Suhaca village and it says that Sifet Barjaktarevic was in charge of all activities. It is in this village that the activities -- the most organised, both paramilitary and every other kind. In the last world war, Suhaca was a prominent Ustasha stronghold. This state body says that Suhaca was well organised, that Sifet Barjaktarevic was the organiser and they were very active. At the top of that page there is a reference to red caps instead of red berets and that there are strong links with the Islamic Religious Community, that criminals are used for the purchasing and transport of weapons and so on and so forth. And you knew nothing of that, although somebody thought that your village had the best possible organisation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Sifet Barjaktarevic was the organiser in my village but he organised the surrender of weapons that people already had, mostly pistols and hunting rifles. And he was the one who organised that. When people set out for Blagaj, he was in favour of heading towards Bosanski Novi or Croatia. There were no other organisations at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many pieces of weaponry were handed over?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. I would say about 300 pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There were 700. You already said there were 700 pieces of weaponry all together and 200 were handed over, which constitutes a difference of 500.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: I never said 700. I said that there were about 300.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's my recollection of 300. So if Mr. Karadzic is saying 700, can he please give me a transcript reference page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've found the reference. This was said when you said that you had hunting rifles, some pistols, and homemade rifles and two semi-automatic rifles that were handed over. All together 300 [In English] in -- of which 70 to 80 were hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 70 to 80 were hunting rifles, and what about the remaining 220? You said that you only had two semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: Yes, most were pistols, handmade rifles, and two semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was it who made their own weapons at home and why?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: This was part of our tradition. A lot of people hang those rifles as decorations on the walls and there were people who knew how to make them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted or will it be considered in the same way as the previous one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: That's what I thought. It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1913, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Sifet Barjaktarevic was a suspect, or rather, that criminal proceedings were instituted against him for his activities in the arming of Suhaca and for possessions of explosives on behalf of the SDA? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ011
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He was actually offered explosives by the SDA. Did you know that Ilija Alibasic offered explosives to Sifet?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D4688. 1D4688. Can we look at the date, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]
